- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is positive and model forecast is below recent 10-day average, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to short-term forecasts.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to lag in recognizing reversal; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment turning points.
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of recent 18-day high unless sentiment is strongly bearish; use sentiment as a filter to prevent extreme pessimism.
